Bug_Title: FL: Do not use floating-point variables as loop counters (FL_FLOATS_AS_LOOP_COUNTERS)
Bug_Details: Using floating-point variables should not be used as loop counters, as they are not precise, which may result in incorrect loops. A loop counter is a variable that is changed with each iteration and controls when the loop should terminate. It is decreased or increased by a fixed amount each iteration. See rule NUM09-J.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by using a floating-point variable 'i' as a loop counter in the for loop. Due to the imprecision of floating-point arithmetic, the loop may not terminate as expected, leading to incorrect results.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method, which uses a floating-point variable as a loop counter. Due to the imprecision of floating-point arithmetic, the loop may not terminate as expected, leading to an incorrect sum value.
